title: Isoscope — the map that maps itself

intro.title: So you always know what your codebase does
intro.sub: how it is architected, what is broken, and what to work on next
intro.proseHTML:
What this is

Isoscope renders a system as an inspectable isometric city: modules are buildings, connections are pipes that know what flows through them, and status is painted on the architecture itself. One JSON spec — or a SQLite graph store your agents maintain as they build — drives everything you see.

This map is isoscope describing itself. The authoring row floats above (spec, store, CLI, MCP, adapters), the engine sits at ground level, and what ships lives below — and the original-web district renders all of it in the browser. Press Stack to see it; click any building or any pipe for its story.

The loop

Open the map on day one of a project. As the codebase grows, agents mirror every module, link, and blocker into the store — and the browser repaints on every change. The map never trails reality.

nodes.name: The spec
nodes.does: One JSON object that describes an entire system: modules, connections, status, levels, and the guided story. Hand-editable, diffable, and the interchange format between every other part.
nodes.built: Schema documented in SPEC.md — 16 keys, all optional except nodes and edges. Two examples ship: this map, and ODIN Sentinel (the first consumer).

nodes.name: Graph store
nodes.does: Plain SQLite shaped as a graph: one row per node, one row per edge — edge attributes live on the edge. The living source of truth agents write to while they work.
nodes.built: bun:sqlite, zero dependencies. Six tables mirror the spec one-to-one; import/export round-trips losslessly.

nodes.name: CLI
nodes.does: Ten verbs: init, import, export, build, serve, ingest, mark, ci, sensor, install-hook. Everything a human, a pipeline, or a non-MCP agent needs to maintain the map from a shell.
nodes.built: TypeScript on Bun, no build step, thin face over lib.ts.

nodes.name: MCP server
nodes.does: Nine tools that let any MCP-capable agent maintain the living map as it builds: upsert modules and links, set status, read the spec, build the artifact, and offer a sensor where a seam has stabilised.
nodes.built: Hand-rolled stdio JSON-RPC — the zero-dependency promise holds even here. Proven end-to-end from the DeepSeek Harness: dsh called iso_overview through its MCP client and got live store data back. Runs under bun only (bun:sqlite), so registrations spawn bun directly rather than npx.

nodes.name: Harness adapters
nodes.does: How each harness is taught to keep the map honest. MCP-capable harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, the DeepSeek Harness) register the server and get the nine tools; harnesses with no MCP client get the same operations as a paste-in CLI contract. Every adapter carries the same working agreement: mirror the codebase in the same session, record what flows, never leave a broken thing unmarked.
nodes.built: DSH.md + dsh.cordis.patch.yml ship the DeepSeek Harness route (cordis insert layer, verified end-to-end against dsh 0.1.1-rc.2). mcp.json is the generic registration. DEEPSEEK.md remains the no-MCP fallback. LUMBR.md is the telemetry bridge: signals in through POST /ci?provider=signal, the remediation scope out through GET /blast-radius.

nodes.name: The engine
nodes.does: The rendered experience: orthographic Three.js city, etched buildings, PCB-routed pipes with escape pins at hubs and schematic junction grammar (dot = joined, arc = crossing), circuit-breaker interaction, three-level stacking, guided trace, single inspector, 18 themes with a runtime contrast floor, live-reload client.
nodes.built: One self-contained template.html. Routing obeys the laws in docs/DESIGN-RULES.md: no transit under strangers, no avoidable same-plane crossings, level-honest risers, R13 escape pins, R16 joint shove, R31 junction grammar.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.does: Injects a spec into the engine template and emits one self-contained HTML file that works from disk — no server, no CORS, nothing to install.
nodes.built: build.ts: importable function + runnable command, ~40 lines.

nodes.name: Live serve
nodes.does: Runs the map in a browser from day one of a project: watches the graph store and repaints on every change — every commit, every agent edit, live.
nodes.built: Bun.serve + SSE + a three-line client in the template. The view survives every repaint (R30 phase 2: the scene rebuilds in place on every store change; camera, stack, theme, inspector, circuit preserved; a new red module still takes the camera). POST /mark and POST /ci accept CI/CD webhooks directly.

nodes.name: The artifact
nodes.does: The shippable output: one HTML file anyone can open, orbit, and interrogate — email it, commit it, host it.
nodes.built: Banner-marked GENERATED; rebuilt from the store in one command.

nodes.name: Examples
nodes.does: Reference specs proving the schema: this self-portrait, ODIN Sentinel's 16-module governance map, and lumbr's 10-module remediation loop.
nodes.built: This map IS examples/isoscope.spec.json — the tool eats its own cooking.

nodes.name: Consumer projects
nodes.does: Any project that adopts the loop: a store in the repo, agents mirroring reality into it, a live map in a browser tab, and an artifact in every release.
nodes.built: ODIN Sentinel is consumer #1 (its architecture map is generated by this engine); lumbr is consumer #2 (examples/lumbr.spec.json, authored from its package graph).

nodes.name: DRC lint & render proof
nodes.does: Keeps the wiring lawful and the render honest. The collision lint scores weighted crossings against the spec's acknowledged budget and fails the build over it; the render proof drives headless Chrome across six viewports; the contrast proof clicks every theme and measures real text/background pairs against WCAG AA, and fails on any JS error.
nodes.built: drc.ts imports the same router.ts the template is built from — one router, never two. scripts/render-proof.ts, overflow-diagnose.ts and contrast-proof.ts speak CDP over a Bun WebSocket, zero deps.

nodes.name: original-web
nodes.does: The main user-facing surface: the isometric codebase-city web app. A Three.js orthographic renderer — modules as buildings with per-face video media surfaces, edges routed by the shared router with circuit-break X marks and advisory state colors, per-module annotations with server write-back, deterministic edge-routing QC, curated theme order, search and paged navigation.
nodes.built: Vite + Three.js, strict TypeScript. src/original-renderer.ts renders this spec; src/annotations.ts keeps per-module notes/files/faces (write-back through the Vite middleware, localStorage fallback); src/edge-qc.ts flags structural routing defects; scripts/edge-layout-qc.ts is the headless QC + layout-optimizer harness (bun). Vitest gates: 16/16.

nodes.name: desert-pants design system
nodes.does: The design system the city is painted with: tokens, 18 themes in light and dark modes, fonts, and the icon set — vendored with a provenance manifest, applied at runtime with a measured WCAG contrast floor.
nodes.built: Vendored under original-web/vendor/desert-pants (CANONICAL-MANIFEST.sha256 + PROVENANCE.md); src/theme-order.ts curates the presented order. okoa.ts is the thin CLI client for the hosted OKOA Design MCP used to work on it upstream.

items.l: round-trip tested against both examples; needs a hostile-input pass
R30 mental-map-stable hot-swap for serve is the next engine rule

Sensor offered — trace boundary at Live serve: the store→browser seam has not moved since 2026-08-22 and every consumer crosses it (events → lumbr://isoscope/serve/*). Accept and an agent installs it; decline with iso_set_sensor.
advisory/2026-09-01-odin holds two more ODIN specs — keep as advisory material or fold into examples
name + public remote are your call

EX-SP.title: Examples prove the schema
EX-SP.carries: Reference specs — living documentation of every key, kept honest because the tool renders them.

SP-DB.title: Spec seeds the store
SP-DB.carries: A full graph import: nodes, edges, status, docs, trace — the JSON decomposed into six tables, losslessly.

MC-DB.title: Agents write the truth
MC-DB.carries: Tool calls from working agents: upserted modules, documented links, status changes — the map staying current with the codebase it describes.

AD-CL.title: Adapters drive the CLI
AD-CL.carries: The same maintenance operations for non-MCP harnesses, expressed as shell commands with an export→edit→import discipline.

DB-CL.title: The store answers the shell
DB-CL.carries: The current graph, exported as spec JSON — for humans, scripts, and diffs.

CL-BU.title: Export feeds the builder
CL-BU.carries: The composed spec object, handed to buildHtml() for injection.

TP-BU.title: The engine is the template
TP-BU.carries: The entire rendered experience — scene, router, inspector, themes — with one slot where the spec lands.

BU-AR.title: One file out
BU-AR.carries: The finished map: engine + spec fused into a single self-contained HTML artifact.

DB-SV.title: The store is watched
DB-SV.carries: File-change events, debounced into SSE pushes — any write to the graph reaches every open browser within a beat.

SV-CO.title: The living map
SV-CO.carries: The freshly-rebuilt map plus a live-reload event stream — the browser tab that stays true all project long.

AR-CO.title: The shipped map
AR-CO.carries: The static artifact for releases, docs, and sharing — same experience, no server.

CO-MC.title: Planned: the loop closes
CO-MC.carries: Consumer projects' agents adopting the contract — every build session ends with the map already updated.

TP-DR.title: One router, linted
TP-DR.carries: The router source itself — injected into the template at build and imported by the lint, so the law the map obeys is the law the lint checks.

SP-OW.title: The spec is the scene
SP-OW.carries: This very file, imported by the renderer — every node, media surface, tag, and status you see in the city.

TP-OW.title: One router, in the browser
TP-OW.carries: The shared router.ts imported straight into the web app — the same laws that route the artifact route the live city, hops and risers included.

DP-OW.title: Painted by desert-pants
DP-OW.carries: Tokens, themes, fonts, and icons flowing into every panel and building — with a runtime contrast floor holding the map readable in all 18 themes.

traceText.EX-SP: A spec exists — maybe written by hand on day one, maybe this very file.
traceText.SP-DB: It seeds the graph store: six tables, one truth.
traceText.MC-DB: From here on, agents maintain it as they build — via MCP tools, mid-session.
traceText.DB-SV: The store is watched; every change becomes an event.
traceText.SV-CO: A browser tab, open from day one, repaints live. You always know.
traceText.DB-CL: The shell can always ask for the current graph…
traceText.AR-CO: That artifact ships with the release.
traceText.CO-MC: And the loop closes: the next session's agents keep the map true.
